card.name: Butoh
card.tagline: Avant-garde 'dance of darkness' born in post-war Japan
card.profile: Butoh is a form of Japanese dance theatre that arose in 1959 through the collaboration of its two founders, Tatsumi Hijikata and Kazuo Ohno (Wikipedia, Butoh). Originally called Ankoku Butoh ('dance of utter darkness'), it features playful and grotesque imagery, taboo subjects, extreme or absurd environments, and is traditionally performed in white body makeup with slow, hyper-controlled motion. The first piece, Kinjiki (Forbidden Colors) by Hijikata - based on Yukio Mishima's novel - premiered at a 1959 dance festival and caused a scandal that established Hijikata as an iconoclast.
card.insight: In Jean Viala and Nourit Masson-Sekine's study, Ohno is regarded as 'the soul of butoh' and Hijikata as 'the architect of butoh'; the form emerged as a deliberate reaction against Japanese dance that Hijikata felt merely imitated the West or Noh (Wikipedia).
